P1.evidence: No setter and no application to read back, so P1a does not apply. The frame ran three parts of four — "understand your current situation, like what you're doing right now, what you have tried in the past and where you're actually trying to get to" — with no "what's in the way" or "what you need". No frame agreement was sought; the rep's next words were "can you hear me?". The open question was never asked: the prospect launched into his own history unprompted.

P2.evidence: Age 51 was volunteered and never asked; height and weight were never established at all. Work was probed properly — "do you sit when you're doing the procedures or are you standing?". Health conditions were never asked as a question; the back history and TRT came out because the prospect offered them, though the rep did follow up with "you been on TRT or not?". Injuries and duration were entirely volunteered. Training week came out unprompted; the rep's only probe was about sports. Results from current training were never asked. Nutrition was asked cleanly — "Tell me more about nutrition... what does it look like for you?". Sleep was attempted but the question "how many hours per day, like usually?" was read as work hours and sleep quality was never covered. Energy was asked well, including "do you feel that you need to like push through the day most of the times?".

P3.evidence: The bridge to the deeper why was the strongest moment of the call — "you feel that you want to get healthier, and I absolutely understand that... However, my question is, why? What's underneath that? What drives you really?" — and the future-state question followed properly: "When you get to this state and physical condition that you aspire to... what's opening up?". The single-goal question was asked but got a null answer ("there's no specific thing that I'm looking for") and the rep did not press for one thing to change. "Who else does that impact?" was never asked; the rep asserted the family benefit himself ("You're showing up better for your family") rather than making the prospect say it, so the drive-through to kids and identity stayed shallow. The reflect-back landed and was confirmed: "Even though you look fit on the outside... you feel fatigued" / "yes, I think you're right".

P4.evidence: The phase was skipped entirely. Nothing was asked about what he had tried, what happened, or why it did not stick. The prospect handed the gap over unprompted twice — "the main reason I don't is because I don't really have a program to follow" and "when you do it on your own like this, you go through ups and downs" — and the rep did not pick either up or convert them into a named root cause.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind. The two-year question, the settle-for question, the why-not and the line-in-the-sand were all absent. The rep moved straight from the reflect-back into the three-pillar presentation. This is the load-bearing omission on this call: when price hesitation arrived the rep had no cost-of-inaction to return to, so the only lever left was the price itself.

P6.evidence: The belief check was run correctly and, to the rep's credit, before any number was said — "do you actually feel that, if we had dialed in all the three things... you would get to your goals?" answered "Yeah, hundred percent". The all-in question was never asked in either pass. When hesitation did surface ("I don't want to commit today") the script calls for a return to Phase 5; instead the rep re-ran the belief check and then went to financial engineering, which is what turned a timing objection into a discount.

P11.evidence: Payment was taken live ("Okay. It says paid"), the Trevor onboarding call was booked for Tuesday 16 June 4:15pm ET, and both emails were confirmed and the agreement signed on the call. But the signature was procedural rather than informed — "Okay, so I signed it. I didn't read it, though" — and when the prospect asked where the top-up term was, the rep could not point to it. The onboarding form was mentioned; the welcome email and the Skool community link were never mentioned at all.

objection_plays.detail: Triggered by "just need to sleep on it for a couple of days". The rep ran the opening moves — the belief question and "what makes you feel that you can?" — and probed how long he had been thinking about it. He did not run "Thinking isn't the problem. Deciding is", the different-decision move, the identity move, or the closing "are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?". It resolved anyway because the prospect self-corrected to a pure money objection: "Maybe I misspoke... it's just really committing the finances".

Isolation ran ("Apart from the finances side, yeah? Let's put that on the side for a second") and consent for the open-wallet conversation ran ("would you be open to have like an honest conversation about the finances?"). Cash on hand was asked and deflected. Everything after that was skipped: monthly left over after bills, number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and crypto/stocks/investments were never asked. The "you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place" reframe was never used. Because the financial picture was never actually built, the rep negotiated against an unverified claim of cash-flow pressure from a dentist running multiple businesses.

A clean OD trigger — "What might have to do is just delay everything for a month and a half... I would probably have to push to mid-July" — and not one scripted move was attempted. No "things never slow down", no "the longer you wait the harder this gets", no "the only thing you can control is right now". The rep answered a timing objection with a price restructure inside roughly ninety seconds.
The wife appears repeatedly in the conversation but never as a decision gate; the prospect treated the purchase as his own call throughout.
No fear or doubt about the modality. He was already using kettlebells and pre-sold on Trevor's content.

Script gap. The prospect asked, twice, for the non-standard structure to be documented — "is that stated somewhere so I don't have to remind someone at that time?" — and there is no play, no clause and no asset for a contract that differs from the standard one. The rep had to fall back on "you have my word on this. The calls are recorded." A second gap: the prospect wanted an instalment plan at no premium ($1,000 x 6) and the only priced instalment carried a $1,200 premium, so the rep improvised a shorter term instead of having an approved option to offer.

notes: Strong rapport and a genuinely good deep-why bridge, sitting on top of two entirely missing phases. Past Attempts and the Consequence Frame were never run, which meant that when the money objection arrived the rep had no leverage other than the price — and he used it, inventing a three-month tier live on the call. Coach the sequence, not the close: run P4 and P5 and the OD play before ever reaching for a number, and never sign a prospect to a contract whose terms differ from what was agreed out loud.
